title: Link ledger — the recorded identity of every re-creatable artefact in a project
description: One file per project (<Project>/.link-ledger.json), written and read by Rules-Guide/link-ledger/link-ledger.mjs. It exists because 'update the artefact, do not recreate it' is invisible in the UI: a trashed-and-recreated doc or tab looks identical to an updated one, while every shared link, bookmark and #gid= reference to it is already dead. Entries are keyed by PURPOSE (kind + key), never by title — a title changes legitimately (dates, rounds), an id must not. This ledger holds real file ids of a real project, so it is a PROJECT artefact and never kit content.

$comment.description: Free annotation. The one reserved instance-level comment field.

version.description: Ledger format version. A reader that does not know the version must refuse rather than guess.

entries.description: One entry per carrier. Order is not meaningful (the writer keeps it sorted by kind+key so a diff stays readable).

kind.description: What the carrier is. `sheet-tab` pairs an `id` (the spreadsheet) with a `gid` (the tab) — both must survive a rebuild, because shared links carry the gid.

key.description: The PURPOSE of the carrier, stable across rebuilds and renames: e.g. `bug-summary/Statistic`, `test-report/doc`, `pagespeed/round-tab`. Two artefacts serving the same purpose in the same project is a contradiction, not two entries.

id.description: The id that must not change: a Drive fileId, a documentId, a report URL slug. This is the whole point of the file.

gid.description: Sheet tab id, where the carrier has one. A rebuilt tab that gets a NEW gid silently kills every shared #gid= link even though the spreadsheet id is unchanged — so a moved gid is a break exactly like a moved id.

title.description: Last seen human title. Informational ONLY — it may drift (dates, rounds) and drift is never a violation.

firstSeen.description: ISO timestamp of the first sighting — the date the promise started.

lastSeen.description: ISO timestamp of the last confirmed match. A carrier nobody has written for a long time is a candidate for review, never an automatic re-point.

adoptions.description: Deliberate re-points (LINK_LEDGER_ADOPT=1), newest last. Kept because a re-point is not an error to be erased: it is a decision someone made, and whoever still holds the old link deserves to be findable in the record.

fromId.description: The id that was abandoned — every link to it is now dead.

fromGid.description: The tab id that was abandoned, where the carrier had one.

reason.description: Why the move was authorised. Optional in the schema, expected in practice: an adoption nobody can explain is indistinguishable from the accident this file exists to catch.
